title: J.X: Partly for any Augsburg Confession — so Pontificii cannot brand alteration and strip Protestants of Religious Peace
pass_a_gloss: Partly for the favor of the Augsburg Confession of whichever form, lest it be charged by the Pontificii [which as it has often been done, so it is done even today] with an alteration of this kind, on account of which Protestants ought to be judged unworthy of the Religious Peace by the Emperor Augustus and the other pontifical Estates of the Empire;
pass_b_english: Partly it was for the Augsburg Confession in either form: so the papal side — as they often have, and still do — cannot charge this kind of alteration, and then say Protestants deserve to lose the Religious Peace before the Emperor and the other papal Estates of the Empire.
source_text: Partim in gratiam Augustanae Confessionis cujuscunque, ne a Pontificiis [quod ut saepe factum, ita hodieque fit] alterationis hujusmodi infimuletur, ob quam Protestantes Pace Religiosa indigni ab Imperatore Augusto aliisque Statibusque Imperii Pontificiis, censeri debeant;

lemmas.gloss: be charged with this kind of alteration
